what_its_for: Rabeprazole reduces the amount of acid your stomach makes. It is used to treat heartburn, acid reflux (GERD), ulcers in the stomach or small intestine, and a condition called Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It may also be used along with antibiotics to treat H. pylori, a type of bacteria that can cause stomach ulcers.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole. Do not crush, chew, or split it, as this can destroy how the medicine works. Take it with or without food, but taking it before a meal (especially breakfast) usually works best. If you are using the sprinkle capsule for children, open the capsule and sprinkle the small pellets onto a small amount of soft food like applesauce or yogurt. Swallow right away without chewing. Do not save the mixture for later.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 20 mg once a day for most conditions. For severe conditions like Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, your doctor may prescribe a higher dose taken twice daily. Always take the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not take more or less than directed. Treatment length can range from a few weeks to several months depending on your condition.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store rabeprazole at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking and drinking alcohol, as both can increase stomach acid and make your condition worse. Avoid foods and drinks that trigger your heartburn, such as spicy foods, citrus fruits, tomato-based products, coffee, chocolate, and fatty meals. Tell your doctor before taking antifungal medicines like ketoconazole or itraconazole, HIV medications like atazanavir or nelfinavir, blood thinners like warfarin, or methotrexate, as rabeprazole can interact with these. Avoid taking extra doses of antacids unless your doctor tells you it is okay.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe or ongoing diarrhea (which could be a sign of a bowel infection), muscle spasms, irregular heartbeat, or seizures (which could mean your magnesium is too low after long-term use), signs of a severe allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing, new or worsening stomach pain, unexplained weight loss, trouble swallowing, or vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds, bone pain, fractures, or unusual bruising if you have been on this medicine for a long time, or symptoms that do not improve after 4 to 8 weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to feel some relief from heartburn and acid symptoms within 1 to 3 days. However, it may take 1 to 4 weeks of regular use to get the full benefit. Keep taking it even if you start to feel better unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): No dose adjustment is usually needed, but your doctor may monitor you more closely for side effects like low magnesium or bone loss with long-term use. Pregnant women: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine during pregnancy. Use it only if the benefit clearly outweighs the risk. Breastfeeding mothers: It is not known if rabeprazole passes into breast milk. Ask your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medicine. Children: The sprinkle capsule form (Aciphex Sprinkle) is approved for children 1 year and older. Tablets are sometimes used in children 12 years and older. Always follow your child's doctor's specific instructions. Kidney or liver problems: If you have severe liver disease, your doctor may prescribe a lower dose or monitor you more carefully. Tell your doctor about all your health conditions before starting this medication.
